about: Massachusetts state grant calls entered by hand from each program's own page: Massachusetts has no state catalog here (docs/state-coverage.md), so this is not a statewide list. All three are Massachusetts Technology Collaborative (MassTech) solicitations. grantmatch/local.py checks this file and turns each entry into a Massachusetts program record; the weekly page watcher rereads every page. Change an entry only from the official page, and update its checked date.

programs.title: Pathmaker Training Provider grants (advanced manufacturing, AI, defense and robotics)
programs.objectives: Direct funding to build and expand training programs that prepare students for careers in advanced manufacturing, AI, defense and robotics. Applicants need at least one industry partner with a direct hiring need.
programs.who: Community-based organizations (including those relying on a fiscal agent), nonprofit entities, workforce development organizations, MassHire boards and career centers, municipalities, community colleges, colleges and universities, comprehensive and vocational high schools, and for-profit companies whose training is open to the public.
programs.application: Read the full requirements and apply from the MassTech page. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
programs.award: The amount isn't stated on the page.
programs.deadlines: Rolling. The page gives an initial deadline of Friday, January 8 and a final FY27 deadline of Friday, April 16; MassTech's list of grant opportunities dates it April 16, 2027.
programs.source_note: The scoring criteria mention matching funds, but the page doesn't say whether a match is required. The full requirements weren't opened.
programs.subjects: Workforce development; Job training; Manufacturing; Artificial intelligence; Robotics; Education

programs.title: Cyber Resilient Massachusetts Grant Program
programs.objectives: Grants toward cybersecurity monitoring and response services (managed detection and response and related services) from CyberTrust Massachusetts.
programs.who: Municipalities, small businesses and nonprofits in Massachusetts. Nonprofits in sectors such as health care and digital health, AI, climate technology, manufacturing and entrepreneur support are given priority.
programs.application: First get a scope of work from CyberTrust Massachusetts, then include it in the application to MassTech.
programs.award: Up to one third of the cost of the CyberTrust Massachusetts services, plus an onboarding fee if there is one, for up to three years. Nonprofits are paid by reimbursement.
programs.match: At least two thirds of the service cost
programs.deadlines: Applications are due on a rolling basis.

programs.title: Technology and Innovation Ecosystem Awards
programs.objectives: Support for capital projects that provide a new technology, business, talent, capital or other support program that adds to growth in the state's technology and innovation sectors.
programs.who: The page says the projects are led by organizations in Massachusetts and doesn't say more about who may apply. Read the solicitation.
programs.application: Applicants are encouraged to tell the Innovation Institute of their interest and are asked to send a preliminary concept paper before a full application.
programs.award: The amount isn't stated on the page. Awards depend on state bond funding being available.
programs.deadlines: Responses are due on a rolling basis.
programs.subjects: Technology; Innovation; Economic development; Capital projects
